raw_response:
I'm 52 years old and I've farmed these 10 mu for 35 years. Never went to school, but this land is my school. My wife and I do the work. Our son works in a factory in town — he sends money but we don't use it for farming. We have to make do with what we have.

It's October now, time to plant wheat. I always plant around October 12th. Too early and the wheat grows too tall before winter and freezes. Too late and the roots don't grow deep enough. I'm using my own seed from last year — I saved the biggest ears from the middle of the field. Why pay for seed when you've got good grain in the bin? I just mix it with that red seed medicine so it doesn't rot in the ground.

Before planting, I hire Old Wang's tractor to plow. Fifty yuan per mu. Expensive, but I can't turn over 10 mu with a hoe anymore. Then I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the kind with three numbers. My father did one bag per mu, I do one bag per mu. It's what I know. In spring, when the wheat starts jointing, I'll put down about 30 jin of urea per mu. Last year I used more but the wheat grew too green and lodged a bit. Also urea got expensive. Maybe 30 jin is enough. Better to save a little money.

I'll water the wheat twice — once after planting if the soil is dry, and once in March or April when it wakes up. Pumping water costs electricity, maybe 30-40 yuan each time. I won't water more unless there's a drought. My neighbor waters four times but he has money. I don't. I spray weed killer once in spring. That's it for poison. I don't like spending on chemicals.

For maize, it goes in the day after wheat comes out — June 10th or 12th usually. There's no time to rest! Maybe five days between harvest and planting. I buy hybrid seed for maize. Can't save it, everyone knows hybrid doesn't breed true. Costs about 40 yuan per mu. At planting I put down fertilizer — almost a bag of compound per mu, maybe a bit less. Then when the maize is knee-high I side-dress some urea. If July and August bring rain, I don't water maize at all. Maybe once at flowering if it's very dry.

My wife and I do all the field work. Our son might come back for wheat harvest, but I can't count on it. For wheat harvest I hire the combine — 60 yuan per mu. We need help carrying bags those days. For maize we mostly do it ourselves, maybe hire a day or two of help.

Last year wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu, maize about 500. I expect the same this year. I'm not trying to get rich. I'm trying to not lose money. If I have a bad year, we still have the corn and my son's wages. That's my insurance.
